paragraphs: Nine fostering services list Stockport as an area they cover, all shown above: Stockport Council's own fostering service and eight independent agencies. The council describes its service as a not-for-profit local authority fostering service with over 300 children in foster placements at any one time. Fostering with the council means caring for Stockport's own children with its social workers behind you; an independent agency recruits, trains and supervises its carers itself and is asked by councils to find homes when they need them.

Need has grown. The council's sufficiency strategy for 2024 to 2027 records 495 children in care in March 2024, up from 362 in 2018, and 342 of them (69.1%) in foster placements. Only 18% of the children it placed with independent agencies lived in Stockport; over 80% were placed in other council areas. The council says there are not enough foster carers across Stockport and Greater Manchester and that it wants more agency carers living in Stockport, particularly for teenagers, brothers and sisters, and disabled children or those with more complex needs. So local carers are wanted whichever service you choose.

Stockport was part of the first Mockingbird pilot in 2015 and has grown to five groups, each a hub home supporting up to ten fostering households with sleepovers, monthly meetings and social activities. Council carers also get a Max Card for days out, free Life Leisure membership and a Blue Light Card. Greater Manchester is the UK's first fostering-friendly city-region, with Stockport Council among the employers offering flexible working and time off for training and for settling a child in.

We do not yet have a Stockport allowance page, so ask the council and two or three of the agencies above to set out what they pay and what support comes with it. If you live near the borough's edges, the Manchester, Tameside, Trafford and Cheshire East pages list more services nearby.
